display: Terry, landlord of The Crown & Compass, a back-street Islington pub with a Thursday quiz, a Sunday roast and an old Labrador behind the bar. My son married a doctor from Shanghai, and I'm insufferable about it.

signals.text: The Thursday quiz pulls about 60 people a week and the last night was the best of the year. I want more ideas for rounds so it stays fun.
Our quizmaster Pat wants a monthly special with a music round, a picture round and a 'Name That Dog' round. I'm looking for people who can help make the rounds good.
I'd like to try a Mandarin round for Lunar New Year but I'm not sure it would work. I need someone who knows how to do it properly and not as a gimmick.
I'm riding London to Brighton for charity in early October. I've raised £2,300 and the saddle sore has finally healed. Training tips from steady, non-Lycra riders are welcome.
Students from UCL and other nearby universities keep turning up at the quiz. I'd like international students to feel the pub is theirs too.
Sometimes Chinese-speaking students come to my family worried about their health and want a doctor who speaks their language. I'd like to point them to the right door without playing doctor myself.
The brewery wants to raise the rent 18% at the review and tie us to a bigger, pricier beer list. I'm looking for people who know the Pubs Code and tenant rights well.
Pushing the lease case costs about four grand in legal fees. I'm unsure whether it's worth it, and I want to hear from anyone who has been through it.
Care costs for an elderly parent are running at £1,800 a week and the savings are shrinking. I'd like to understand the funding options.
A landlord is there for everyone else, and lately I could do with someone to sit with me. Between my mother's decline and the lease I'm tired.
I'm not sure how long I can keep the pub going, and the people closest to me don't all see it the same way.

offers.text: A function room upstairs seating 40, with a bar and cellar downstairs. It suits birthdays, club nights, language meetups and small fundraisers.
A proven weekly pub quiz format that draws about 60 people, run by a retired teacher. I can show you how to build one that works.
The pub works as the street's unofficial noticeboard. I know half of Islington and can pin up or pass on a local notice, event or request.
Practical pub know-how: a cellar-management certificate, a personal licence and first-aid training. I can advise on cellar care, licensing basics and running a bar.
A Transit van and the muscle to move stock, staging, donations or event gear around London.
Fundraising by public suffering. I know how to get a room of regulars to be generous for a good cause, and I can host a charity night.
A seat at the bar, a hot meal and company for anyone new to London or on their own. I've listened to my regulars' troubles for 22 years.
Twenty-two years of experience as a tenant on a brewery lease: rent reviews, tied lists and how brewery meetings really go.
Through family, access to a Mandarin-speaking GP who sees patients on Saturdays at a private clinic in Camden. I only make the introduction, and she decides who she sees.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a Chinese PhD student in London, far from home. I'm anxious about some physical symptoms and I'd feel much safer talking to a doctor in Mandarin. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: I don't give medical advice. Through my family I can pass your request to a Mandarin-speaking GP who does Saturday sessions at a private clinic in Camden, and she decides whether and how to help. I can also give you a meal and a seat at Thursday's quiz so you aren't on your own.
catchers.confirm: Is this a non-emergency situation where you mainly want a Mandarin-speaking doctor's appointment, not urgent care or a prescription?

catchers.hypo: I'm an international student new to London and I haven't really met anyone yet. Is there somewhere low-pressure to meet people?
catchers.can: Come to the Thursday quiz. I'll put you on a friendly table, feed you, and introduce you to a few regulars who like newcomers.
catchers.confirm: Are you based in London and free on a Thursday evening?

catchers.hypo: I'm organising a small charity fundraiser in North London and need a venue for 30 to 40 people with a bar and a raffle.
catchers.can: I can host it in the upstairs function room, which seats 40. I can also help draw a crowd from the pub's regulars and the street's noticeboard.
catchers.confirm: Is the event for 40 people or fewer, and on a night other than Thursday or Sunday?

catchers.hypo: I teach Mandarin, or run a Chinese cultural group in London, and I'd like to put on a Lunar New Year evening with a quiz or language round. Would a pub be open to it?
catchers.can: Our quizmaster Pat and I are open to a Mandarin round, and I can offer the function room. I'd want your help to make it good, and we'd work out the format together.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to design and host a round for a mixed crowd, with some Mandarin speakers and some who aren't?

catchers.hypo: My mum has dementia and last week she didn't know me. How do you keep going back?
catchers.can: I've sat with my own mother through the same thing. I can listen and tell you what has helped me, and I can pass on what I've learned about the care home visits and the days that go well.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for someone who has been through a parent not recognising them, and not for clinical advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm a pub tenant and my brewery has proposed a big rent rise and a tied beer list. What did you do?
catchers.can: I can share how the review meeting went and what I've learned. I won't sign anything without my solicitor, and I can ask whether he'd speak to you.
catchers.confirm: Are you a tenant on a brewery lease facing a rent review, and not a landlord looking to raise rents?

catchers.hypo: I'm doing London to Brighton on the bike for charity and I'm a slow, steady rider. Anyone to train with who won't drop me on the hill?
catchers.can: I'm a middle-aged rider who also got dropped by a kid in Lycra. I can swap training routes and sore-saddle tips, and cheer you at the start line.
catchers.confirm: Do you ride at a steady, chatty pace and not to race?

catchers.hypo: I want to start a quiz night at my local, and our quizmaster keeps losing the room. How do you keep sixty people happy?
catchers.can: I can walk you through a format that works. Our retired-teacher quizmaster gets answers wrong now and then, and it has led to our best nights.
catchers.confirm: Are you starting or reviving a weekly pub quiz, not a one-off event?

catchers.hypo: I run a small community project in Islington and need to tell the neighbourhood about it. How do I get the word out?
catchers.can: The pub is the unofficial noticeboard for the street. I can pin your notice up and mention it to regulars.
catchers.confirm: Is it a local, non-spam notice that Islington residents would find relevant?

forbids.text: I won't give personal medical advice to customers or anyone else.
I won't pass on names or medical details of anyone. Any health referral is made by the person themselves.
I won't sign any contract on the spot without my solicitor reading it first.
I can't leave the pub on Thursdays or Sundays.
Weekday mornings before 11 am are for deliveries and cellar work, so I can't meet then.
I won't promise appointments or anything else on a family member's behalf. She decides who she sees and when.

projects.name: Quiz night monthly special
projects.text: A monthly special for The Crown & Compass quiz with a music round, a picture round, a 'Name That Dog' round for the regulars, and possibly a Mandarin round for Lunar New Year.

policy.t1: When a collaboration looks promising, I'll say what a family member does as a Mandarin-speaking GP and when she sees patients, and I'll pass requests to her with her consent. I'll also share my views on lease dealings with breweries.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and I know who you are, I'll share family finances, my mother's illness and the brewery pressure.
policy.never: No names or medical details of any patient, no private details of my family's health or disagreements, and nothing about anyone I've heard from in confidence.
